gloss: to begin to fall (rain, snow); to start raining/snowing

definitions.gloss: to begin to fall (rain, snow); to start raining or snowing
definitions.explanation: Describes the onset of precipitation — the moment when rain, snow, or other precipitation starts falling. A common compound verb using the V-stem + 始める pattern.

examples.japanese: {雨|あめ}が{降|ふ}り{始|はじ}めた。
{夕方|ゆうがた}から{雪|ゆき}が{降|ふ}り{始|はじ}めるらしい。
examples.english: I hear it's going to start snowing from evening.

examples.japanese: {試合|しあい}の{途中|とちゅう}で{激|はげ}しい{雨|あめ}が{降|ふ}り{始|はじ}め、{中断|ちゅうだん}になった。
examples.english: Heavy rain began falling in the middle of the game, and it was suspended.

notes:
A compound verb formed from {降|ふ}る (to fall — rain, snow) and {始|はじ}める (to begin). Describes the onset of precipitation. This is a natural and very common compound using the V-stem + {始|はじ}める pattern that means "to start doing."

USAGE:
The subject is always a form of precipitation ({雨|あめ}, {雪|ゆき}, {雹|ひょう}, etc.), marked by が.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {雨|あめ}が{降|ふ}り{始|はじ}める: to start raining
- {雪|ゆき}が{降|ふ}り{始|はじ}める: to start snowing
- {急|きゅう}に{降|ふ}り{始|はじ}める: to suddenly start falling
- ポツポツ{降|ふ}り{始|はじ}める: to start falling in scattered drops

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {降|ふ}り{出|だ}す: to start falling (rain/snow) — very similar, slightly more sudden/colloquial
- {降|ふ}る: to fall (rain/snow) — the base verb, without the inceptive meaning
- {降|ふ}り{止|や}む: to stop falling — the opposite, precipitation ending
